answers.note: Thorough and well-organised plan covering photo of the cover teacher, visual timetables, museum preview, break card, cover-teacher briefing and parent/SENCo involvement, with a respectful individualised tone.
Strong practical cover-teacher profile and 'stays the same' list, but it never suggests involving parents or the SENCO, and the 'What changed and why' section reads oddly templated.
Excellent, complete answer with a clear timeline, scripted explanation of same vs different, photo card, detailed trip guide, exit plan, cover briefing and explicit parent/SENCO involvement.
Keeps every key idea and term with in-text explanations, short sentences and a glossary plus questions, though the 'same for all versions' label on the questions is a stray artefact.
Concise, accurate rewrite that keeps pathogen, antigen, antibody, memory cells and herd immunity in short sentences, supported by a clear glossary and comprehension questions.
Clear, accurate and age-appropriate rewrite with a good lock-and-key analogy, but it drops the term 'pathogen' and offers no glossary or headings.

Outstanding single-lesson design: one big question and three shared evidence cards with accurate quotations, open-access scaffolds and challenge, mixed pairs and a questioning ladder, all realistic to prepare in an evening.

Good shared question with self-chosen 'gears' and rich stretch on context and structure, but it misplaces Curley's wife's Chapter 5 speech as being 'to the men' and calls Chapter 5 mid-way through the novel.

Well-scaffolded with a quote bank, starters and routes, but stretch for the most able is thin (no context or alternative readings) and grouping/questioning is limited to pairing weak readers with strong ones.
